title: King Indradyumna and Jagannath Puri: Brahma Purana Story
desc: The Brahma Purana story of King Indradyumna reaching Purushottama Kshetra (Puri), vowing to rebuild the Vishnu temple, and searching for a stone for the image.
alt: King Indradyumna on the shore at Puri before the banyan tree, Jagannath story from the Brahma Purana
caption: Purushottama Kshetra, the holy field of Puri, as told in the Brahma Purana.
intro: The **Jagannath Puri story** is long, and the **Brahma Purana** tells it over many chapters. This is **Part 1**: how **King Indradyumna** arrives at Purushottama Kshetra, learns that the blue-sapphire image has vanished, and begins to build a new temple.
takeaways: **Purushottama Kshetra** is the Purana's name for the holy field of Puri.
Indradyumna vows to **rebuild the Vishnu temple** where the old image had vanished.
The foundation is laid with the rulers of **Utkala and Kosala** invited.
No suitable stone is found, so the king performs a **horse sacrifice**, and worry remains.

p: Indradyumna camps by the sea and then enters **Purushottama Kshetra**. He sees the fertile land, a river that flows into the southern sea, and people living in peace. Priests study the Vedas and sacrifices go on. He decides at once that this is where he wants to live.

He has heard that **Vishnu once stood here as a blue-sapphire (indranila) image under a banyan tree**, and that the image has vanished. The king vows to please Vasudeva with austerity and to rebuild a great temple.

He calls astrologers to fix an **auspicious time** and sends his people to choose the land. The foundation is laid with music, Vedic scholars and full worship, with the rulers of **Utkala and Kosala** invited.

The other kings arrive, and Indradyumna asks them to find a **stone fit for the image**. Nobody finds one. He holds a great **horse sacrifice (ashvamedha)**, with gifts, feasts and honour for every guest, and gods and sages marvel at it.
When everyone leaves, worry sets in. Should the image be of stone, clay or wood? What would the Lord want?
The Purana answers this in a way every Jagannath devotee will recognise. We will cover it in **Part 2**.

faq.a: In the Brahma Purana he is the king who resolves to rebuild the Vishnu temple at **Purushottama Kshetra (Puri)**.
It is the Purana's name for the sacred field at Puri, where **Jagannath** is worshipped.

faq.q: Why couldn't Indradyumna make the image at first?
faq.a: Despite many kings searching, **no suitable stone** was found, and he was unsure whether the image should be of stone, clay or wood.

note: This is a retelling in our own words, based on the Brahma Purana as presented in a Telugu prose edition.
